- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Forecast tends to lag 1–2 days behind true price movements — adjust forward-looking forecasts by +0.5–1.5% for each lagged day.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >70% spike) — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is rising steadily, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope by 10–20% in early horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (±10% from 14-day moving average) — cap or clip forecasts to prevent volatility overfitting.
